tagline: From a silver town through mountain forests to tundra above timberline
intro: Guanella Pass Road crosses the steep divide between the Clear Creek and South Platte watersheds, climbing from creekside forests through broad meadows to tundra above timberline. It is a Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway and a National Forest Scenic Byway. Colorado DOT presents its succession of environments as a lesson in Rocky Mountain ecosystems and lists a one-hour drive over 22 miles. At lower elevations, spruce, fir, aspen and pine line cascading creeks; higher meadows provide habitat for beavers and nesting birds.

The crossing passes through an old logging and mining area. At its northern end, Georgetown began during the 1859 gold rush; the discovery of silver in 1864 started the local silver boom. The pass received its name in 1953, honoring Byron Guanella, a Clear Creek County road supervisor and commissioner for nearly 50 years.

From Georgetown in the Clear Creek valley, the road heads south to the pass, then descends toward Grant in the Geneva Creek valley. The route is paved all the way to U.S. 285. At the crest, trails branch east toward Mount Bierstadt and west toward Square Top Mountain. The southern end reaches Grant at the mouth of Geneva Creek, where the creek joins the North Fork South Platte.

moments.title: Georgetown
moments.text: Georgetown began with gold, but silver gave the town its mining boom. Gold was discovered here in 1859; the larger silver discovery followed in 1864. Georgetown became a center for thousands of miners working the surrounding hills. The town stretches along Clear Creek, with its historic downtown at the southern, upper end. Preserved buildings from the silver boom belong to a National Historic Landmark district that also includes Silver Plume and the railroad park between the two towns. The district preserves mining structures as well as town buildings.

moments.title: Guanella Pass
moments.text: The road reaches open tundra above timberline at Guanella Pass. Below the crest, streams wind through broad meadows; lower still, spruce, fir, aspen and pine grow along cascading creeks. Trails leave the summit eastward for Mount Bierstadt and westward for Square Top Mountain. Bierstadt takes its name from German-American landscape painter Albert Bierstadt, who made the first recorded ascent in 1863. Its trail first descends into the marshlands of Scott Gomer Creek before climbing the mountain’s western slopes. Cairns mark the ascent toward a relatively flat area below the main summit block.

moments.title: Grant
moments.text: Geneva Creek reaches the North Fork South Platte at Grant, beside U.S. 285. The creek rises at the Continental Divide west of Mount Bierstadt and descends southeast through a canyon. Its valley carries the byway toward this southern junction. Grant is an unincorporated community in the Front Range foothills, with a retired general store, post office, houses and trailers between the highway and river. County Road 62 follows Geneva Creek north from here toward the pass and Georgetown.

practical: Guanella Pass: The road closes seasonally on or about November 26 and reopens Memorial Day weekend, with closure points at Naylor Lake and Burning Bear Campground. (checked 2026-10-11)
